| `src/models/omnilearned/utils.py` | `get_model_parameters` plus a replacement for the unsafe partial checkpoint loader |
| `src/scripts/train.py` | `create_omnilearned_model`, `prepare_batch_omnilearned`, `zero_muon_kinematics`, medium-backbone freeze policy, learning-rate schedule and seed policy |
| `src/dataset/preprocessing.py` | four-momentum conversion, dE/dx transform, coordinate/time scaling, PID assignment, overflow aggregation, globals and truth preparation |
| `src/dataset/dataloader.py` | pad/truncate, collate and `pid`/`add_info`/`cond` assembly |
| `src/constants/dataset.py` | `GLOBAL_COND_BASE_DIM = 10` |

Gregor's presets use four learned readout tokens and MLP ratio two:

| Preset | base dimension | heads | body blocks | head blocks |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| small | 128 | 8 | 8 | 2 |
| medium | 512 | 16 | 12 | 2 |
| large | 1024 | 32 | 28 | 4 |

The audited MINERvA defaults are four kinematic inputs, five auxiliary token
features, conditional width 10, PID width 8, coordinate dimension 2,
`use_pid=True`, no local/global interaction block, LHC interaction type,
KNN `K=10`, and classifier/regression mode as appropriate.

## Exact tensor contract

`PET2.forward(x, y, cond=None, pid=None, add_info=None)` expects:

| Tensor | Shape | Dtype | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | `(B,N,4)` | float32 | eta, phi, `log(pT+1e-6)`, `log(E+1e-6)` |
| `pid` | `(B,N)` | int64 | upstream raw object/PID category 0–7 |
| `add_info` | `(B,N,5)` | float32 | transformed dE/dx, x/1e4, y/1e4, z/1e4, time/1e4 |
| `cond` | `(B,10)` or manifest-bound 13/16-wide extension | float32 | reconstructed global block; stored width and `--include-E-sum` must agree |
| `y` | `(B,)` | long/float | task label; never a reco-side OmniFold input |

The pinned dataloader pads or truncates a batch to the first 33 tokens without
an energy re-sort, even though preprocessing can retain up to 150 tokens by
default. Token ordering and both limits are therefore checkpoint inputs. The
body adds PID and auxiliary embeddings, prepends one conditional token, then
prepends four learned readout tokens. The classifier first runs its
`TokenAttBlock` head stack, flattens the four readout tokens, and applies its
MLP. Regression yields one logit; upstream classification yields
`len(task.class_idx)` logits. The OmniFold adapter requires the one-logit
binary-ratio head.

The prepared global block can be 16-wide while `ol_num_cond` defaults to 10;
the training code also accepts widths 10, 13, or 16 through a permissive
branch. A compatibility manifest must bind the stored conditional width,
feature ordering, `ol_num_cond`, and `--include-E-sum` together. A width
mismatch is fatal rather than a tolerated semantic variant.

The checkpoint is a two-level mapping. The future manifest must enumerate
every top-level component and every inner state-dict key and shape. Important
inner prefixes are:

- `checkpoint["body"]`: `embed.*`, `local_physics.*`,
  `cond_embed.0.*`, `add_embed.0.*`, `pid_embed.0.weight`, `token`,
  `in_blocks.{i}.*`, and `norm.*`;
- `checkpoint["body"]`: `interaction.*` only when `use_int=True`; these keys
  are absent under the audited MINERvA default;
- `checkpoint["classifier_head"]`: `in_blocks.{i}.*`, `fc.*`, and `out.*`;
- `checkpoint["generator_head"]`: only when the task/configuration actually
  instantiates the generator head.

`DynamicTanh` contributes `alpha` and `weight`, with no bias.
`nn.MultiheadAttention` was created with `bias=False`, so attention projection
bias keys must not be invented.

## MINERvA adapter boundary

The adapter may consume only symmetric reconstructed signal/data/background
objects for Step 1. It must build muon, photon, blob, prong and overflow
tokens under one documented reconstruction vocabulary. Truth labels,
interaction categories and prepared MC task labels remain bookkeeping or
Step-2-only information.

The pinned transforms include:

- eta clipped to `[-10,10]`;
- phi from `atan2(py,px)`;
- `log(pT+1e-6)` and `log(E+1e-6)` in the declared raw units;
- dE/dx as `log(abs(value)+0.1)` after sentinel handling and clipping;
- position and time divided by 10000;
- global calorimetry, passive recoil, Michel count, reco-muon presence,
  gamma-gamma mass, charged-pion-prong count, and per-category energy sums.

Units, missing values, type vocabulary, overflow conservation, token ordering,
and masks must be receipt-bound independently for signal, data and literal
backgrounds. Gregor's prepared public `.pb` rows cannot satisfy this boundary:
they lack the data/background/miss legs, physics weights and stable event
identity required by OmniFold.

## Two incompatible compatibility paths

### L: legacy-exact reproduction

`gregor-pet2-legacy-exact-v1` reproduces the pinned forward behavior,
including its known hazards:

1. real muon PID 0 collides with `padding_idx=0`;
2. padding is inferred from transformed `log(pT) != 0`;
3. a muon-kinematics ablation may therefore remove the token.

It may strictly load an exactly matching legacy checkpoint, subject to the
constructibility boundary below. Its purpose is reproduction/provenance
diagnosis only. It is not eligible for physics conclusions or publication
OmniFold.

### K: corrected compatibility

`gregor-pet2-corrected-v1` must:

- reserve PID 0 for padding, shift every real PID by one, and widen the
  embedding from 8 to 9 entries;
- pass an explicit boolean token mask through body and heads;
- choose and receipt whether a muon ablation keeps a blank-but-present token
  or removes it.

The mask correction preserves parameter shapes but changes forward semantics.
The PID correction changes only `pid_embed.0.weight`. A permitted,
information-preserving migration is:

```text
new[0] = 0
new[1:9] = old[0:8]
```

Every other tensor must load with an exact key and shape. The migration
receipt must enumerate loaded, remapped, skipped and mismatched keys.
Unlisted skips or mismatches are fatal.

L and K have distinct architecture/preprocessing fingerprints, output
namespaces and experimental cells. Their results may not be pooled.

## Advertised-checkpoint availability boundary

The only advertised artifacts found in the inspected source are
`best_model_pretrain_s.pt` and `best_model_pretrain_m.pt`. They are generic
OmniLearned jet-pretrained weights, not published MINERvA-fine-tuned
checkpoints. No MINERvA-fine-tuned weight artifact was found.

The upstream MINERvA path historically consumed those generic artifacts
through a shape-filtered partial load. That was necessary because the target
configuration can differ in PID width (`ol_pid_dim=8` versus PET2's default
9), `input_dim=4`, `add_dim=5`, and `cond_dim=10/13/16`. Consequently
`pid_embed`, `embed`, `add_embed`, and `cond_embed` may never have transferred;
the exact surviving keys are unknown.

If an advertised artifact does not exactly match the frozen L schema, the
strict L-P cell is **unconstructible**. The acceptable paths are:

1. obtain a licensed, hash-bound, exactly matching checkpoint; or
2. run an explicitly named diagnostic partial-transfer cell whose complete
   loaded/skipped/mismatched key inventory and loaded-parameter fraction are
   receipted and which is forbidden from carrying initialization evidence.

The diagnostic cell is not L-P or K-P and may not be promoted by relabeling.
The loaded-parameter fraction and exact key set must be reported before any
transfer result is interpreted.

## Strict checkpoint manifest

Every field below is required before weight bytes are opened:

```text
source_repo_url
source_commit_sha
vendored_files[] {path, sha256, upstream_url, license, copyright_holder}
architecture_variant
architecture_config
architecture_fingerprint
hazard_policy {pid_shift, mask_source, muon_ablation_policy}
preprocessing_revision
preprocessing_fingerprint
tensor_schema
categorical_vocabulary
state_dict_schema {top_level_keys, per_key_shapes, dtypes}
load_receipt_schema {load_mode, terminal_state, loaded, remapped, skipped,
                     mismatched, parameter_fraction}
checkpoint_sha256
checkpoint_size_bytes
weight_license
weight_redistribution_permitted
weight_provenance {url, publisher, retrieved_at, retrieved_sha256}
framework_versions
determinism_policy {seed, deterministic_algorithms, cudnn_policy}
safe_loading_policy
```

The loader must:

- verify size and SHA-256 before deserialization;
- use safetensors when available, or `torch.load(weights_only=True)` only for
  a declared legacy artifact;
- reject pickle execution;
- reject missing, extra or wrong-shaped tensors;
- forbid `strict=False`, heuristic transpose, random fallback, or an
  unreceipted partial load;
- reject a checkpoint whose architecture family differs from the requested
  backend;
- bind `load_mode` to either `strict` or `diagnostic_partial`;
- return only `eligible`, `diagnostic_only`, or `unavailable` with exact
  reasons. `diagnostic_only` is valid only for `diagnostic_partial`, and may
  never be relabeled as `eligible`.

Gregor's current `_filter_partial_state` silently drops output tensors and
shape mismatches. It must not be used for evidence-bearing transfer.

## Matched future experiment

Architecture, preprocessing and initialization must be separated:

| Cell | Architecture | Preprocessing | Initialization |
|---|---|---|---|
| L-R | legacy exact | pinned legacy | random |
| L-P [availability boundary](#advertised-checkpoint-availability-boundary) | legacy exact | pinned legacy | strictly compatible checkpoint |
| K-R | corrected | pinned/corrected receipt | random |
| K-P | corrected | pinned/corrected receipt | checkpoint plus explicit PID remap |
| K-R′ | corrected | one declared preprocessing variant | random |

Required negative controls are shape-preserving tensor permutation,
random initialization matched to checkpoint tensor statistics, and a
separately labeled trunk-only transfer. Loaded parameter fractions and exact
key sets are mandatory. Full fine-tuning and frozen-body fine-tuning are
different cells.

Only L-P minus L-R, or K-P minus K-R, on identical rows, seeds and budgets can
speak to initialization—and only if the weight license, checksum and negative
controls pass. No such evidence currently exists.

## Licensing and unresolved checkpoint facts

`gregorkrz/minerva-ml` is MIT-licensed. The upstream
`ViniciusMikuni/OmniLearned` project declares MIT in `pyproject.toml` but has
no standalone LICENSE file at the inspected revision; a vendored
implementation must preserve both projects' notices and attribution. The
public dataset is CC-BY-4.0. HyperScale is unavailable with unverifiable
licensing and is excluded.

The raw ingestion script hard-imports ROOT/PyROOT, whose LGPL/GPL obligations
are separate from the MIT model code. A clean integration should consume an
already authorized dataset or independently implement only the documented
array transforms, avoiding a vendored copy of the ROOT ingestion path unless
its licensing and distribution obligations are reviewed explicitly.

The advertised generic checkpoint files remain inaccessible and have no
verified artifact license or checksum. No MINERvA-fine-tuned checkpoint is
published. A real manifest or author response is still needed to establish:

- released PID dimension and exact input/additional/conditional widths;
- which keys actually survived Gregor's historical partial loader;
- pretraining interaction-block and head configuration;
- checkpoint SHA-256, size, license and redistribution permission;
- exact preprocessing units and conditional feature width;
- whether PID-0/padding and muon-ablation behaviors were intended.

Until all are resolved, arm F remains `unavailable`; building this design does
not change that status.

   188	def _pair_rows(
   189	    dataset: CanonicalDataset, *, split_seed: int
   190	) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
   191	    signal = dataset.signal
   192	    partitions = stable_partition(
   193	        signal.reco.row_index,
   194	        split_seed,
   195	        (0.7, 0.15, 0.15),
   196	        identity=signal.event_key,
   197	    )
   198	    truth_mu_pt = signal.truth.globals[
   199	        :, signal.truth.global_names.index("mu_pt")
   200	    ]
   201	    pairs: list[np.ndarray] = []
   202	    hidden = np.zeros(signal.reco.n_rows, dtype=np.int8)
   203	    for partition in range(3):
   204	        rows = np.flatnonzero(signal.pass_reco & (partitions == partition))
   205	        order = rows[np.argsort(truth_mu_pt[rows], kind="mergesort")]
   206	        count = len(order) // 2
   207	        lower = order[:count]
   208	        upper = order[-count:]
   209	        hidden[lower] = -1
   210	        hidden[upper] = 1
   211	        pairs.append(np.column_stack((lower, upper)))
   212	    pair_rows = np.concatenate(pairs, axis=0).astype(np.int64)
   213	    if pair_rows.shape[0] < 100:
   214	        raise ValueError("conditional stress fixture has too few split-local pairs")
   215	    return pair_rows, hidden, partitions

   218	def _shuffle_carrier(
   219	    hidden: np.ndarray,
   220	    paired_rows: np.ndarray,
   221	    partitions: np.ndarray,
   222	    *,
   223	    seed: int,
   224	) -> tuple[np.ndarray, float, dict[str, float]]:
   225	    carrier = hidden.copy()
   226	    paired = paired_rows.reshape(-1)
   227	    labels = hidden[paired] > 0
   228	    for attempt in range(1000):
   229	        candidate = hidden.copy()
   230	        for partition in range(3):
   231	            rows = paired[partitions[paired] == partition]
   232	            rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 1009 * attempt + partition)
   233	            candidate[rows] = candidate[rows][rng.permutation(len(rows))]
   234	        auc = _auc(labels, candidate[paired])
   235	        by_partition = {
   236	            str(partition): _auc(
   237	                labels[partitions[paired] == partition],
   238	                candidate[paired][partitions[paired] == partition],
   239	            )
   240	            for partition in range(3)
   241	        }
   242	        if abs(auc - 0.5) <= 0.02 and all(
   243	            abs(value - 0.5) <= 0.02 for value in by_partition.values()
   244	        ):
   245	            return candidate, auc, by_partition
   246	    raise RuntimeError("failed to construct a chance carrier shuffle")

   249	def _assign_carrier(
   250	    batch: TokenBatch,
   251	    family: str,
   252	    carrier_sign: np.ndarray,
   253	    paired_rows: np.ndarray,
   254	) -> TokenBatch:
   255	    continuous = batch.continuous.copy()
   256	    coords = batch.coords.copy()
   257	    mask = batch.token_mask.copy()
   258	    type_id = batch.type_id.copy()
   259	    view_id = batch.view_id.copy()
   260	    globals_ = batch.globals.copy()
   261	    overflow = (
   262	        None if batch.overflow_energy is None else batch.overflow_energy.copy()
   263	    )
   264	    muon_cont = (
   265	        None if batch.muon_continuous is None else batch.muon_continuous.copy()
   266	    )
   267	    muon_coords = None if batch.muon_coords is None else batch.muon_coords.copy()
   268	    muon_present = (
   269	        None if batch.muon_present is None else batch.muon_present.copy()
   270	    )
   271	    rows = paired_rows.reshape(-1)
   272	    for row in rows:
   273	        valid = np.flatnonzero(mask[row] & (type_id[row] != TYPE_OVERFLOW))
   274	        if len(valid) < 2:
   275	            raise ValueError("conditional carrier requires at least two retained tokens")
   276	        first = valid[0]
   277	        sign = int(carrier_sign[row])
   278	        if family == "view":
   279	            view_id[row, mask[row]] = 1
   280	            view_id[row, first] = VIEW_U if sign > 0 else VIEW_V
   281	        elif family == "type":
   282	            type_id[row, mask[row]] = TYPE_RECO_CLUSTER
   283	            type_id[row, first] = TYPE_TRACK if sign > 0 else TYPE_RECO_CLUSTER
   284	        elif family == "rich":
   285	            globals_[row, batch.global_names.index("vertex_z")] = float(sign)
   286	        elif family == "muon-token":
   287	            if muon_coords is None or muon_cont is None or muon_present is None:
   288	                raise ValueError("muon carrier fields are unavailable")
   289	            midpoint = max(1, len(valid) // 2)
   290	            left = valid[:midpoint]
   291	            right = valid[midpoint:]
   292	            coords[row, left] = np.asarray([0.0, 0.0], dtype=np.float32)
   293	            continuous[row, left, 0] = 0.75
   294	            if len(right):
   295	                coords[row, right] = np.asarray([4.0, 0.0], dtype=np.float32)
   296	                continuous[row, right, 0] = 2.25
   297	            muon_coords[row] = (
   298	                np.asarray([3.95, 0.0], dtype=np.float32)
   299	                if sign > 0
   300	                else np.asarray([0.05, 0.0], dtype=np.float32)
   301	            )
   302	            muon_present[row] = True
   303	        elif family == "overflow":
   304	            last = mask.shape[1] - 1
   305	            mask[row, last] = True
   306	            type_id[row, last] = TYPE_OVERFLOW
   307	            view_id[row, last] = VIEW_AGGREGATE
   308	            continuous[row, last] = 0.0
   309	            continuous[row, last, 0] = 1.5 if sign > 0 else 0.5
   310	            coords[row, last] = 0.0
   311	            if overflow is None:
   312	                raise ValueError("overflow evidence array is unavailable")
   313	            overflow[row] = continuous[row, last, 0]
   314	        else:  # pragma: no cover - guarded by public entry point
   315	            raise ValueError(f"unknown conditional carrier: {family}")
   316	    return replace(
   317	        batch,
   318	        continuous=continuous,
   319	        coords=coords,
   320	        token_mask=mask,
   321	        type_id=type_id,
   322	        view_id=view_id,
   323	        globals=globals_,
   324	        overflow_energy=overflow,
   325	        muon_continuous=muon_cont,
   326	        muon_coords=muon_coords,
   327	        muon_present=muon_present,
   328	        provenance=f"{batch.provenance}|conditional_carrier={family}",
   329	    ).validated()

   332	def _decode_carrier(batch: TokenBatch, family: str, rows: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
   333	    decoded = np.empty(len(rows), dtype=np.int8)
   334	    for index, row in enumerate(rows):
   335	        valid = np.flatnonzero(
   336	            batch.token_mask[row] & (batch.type_id[row] != TYPE_OVERFLOW)
   337	        )
   338	        first = valid[0]
   339	        if family == "view":
   340	            decoded[index] = 1 if batch.view_id[row, first] == VIEW_U else -1
   341	        elif family == "type":
   342	            decoded[index] = 1 if batch.type_id[row, first] == TYPE_TRACK else -1
   343	        elif family == "rich":
   344	            decoded[index] = (
   345	                1
   346	                if batch.globals[row, batch.global_names.index("vertex_z")] > 0
   347	                else -1
   348	            )
   349	        elif family == "muon-token":
   350	            decoded[index] = 1 if batch.muon_coords[row, 0] > 2.0 else -1
   351	        elif family == "overflow":
   352	            decoded[index] = 1 if batch.overflow_energy[row] > 1.0 else -1
   353	        else:  # pragma: no cover
   354	            raise ValueError(f"unknown carrier family: {family}")
   355	    return decoded

   358	def _background_carrier(
   359	    batch: TokenBatch, family: str
   360	) -> TokenBatch:
   361	    rows = np.arange(batch.n_rows, dtype=np.int64)
   362	    if len(rows) % 2:
   363	        rows = rows[:-1]
   364	    paired = rows.reshape(-1, 2)
   365	    carrier = np.zeros(batch.n_rows, dtype=np.int8)
   366	    carrier[paired[:, 0]] = -1
   367	    carrier[paired[:, 1]] = 1
   368	    if len(paired):
   369	        batch = _assign_carrier(batch, family, carrier, paired)
   370	    return batch

     3	This is a clean implementation of general point-edge/attention ideas.  It does
     4	not copy Gregor Krzmanc's or OmniLearned source.  Every padding decision is

    44	    def validated(self) -> "ModelConfig":
    45	        if min(self.continuous_dim, self.coord_dim, self.global_dim) < 1:
    46	            raise ValueError("model input dimensions must be positive")

    70	    class _EdgeBlock(nn.Module):
    71	        def __init__(self, dim: int, k_neighbors: int):
    72	            super().__init__()
    73	            self.k_neighbors = k_neighbors
    74	            self.edge_mlp = nn.Sequential(
    75	                nn.Linear(2 * dim, dim),
    76	                nn.GELU(),
    77	                nn.Linear(dim, dim),
    78	            )
    79	            self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(dim)
    80	
    81	        def forward(self, h, coords, mask):
    82	            batch, tokens, dim = h.shape
    83	            k = min(self.k_neighbors, max(tokens - 1, 1))
    84	            distance = torch.cdist(coords, coords)
    85	            valid_pairs = mask[:, :, None] & mask[:, None, :]
    86	            eye = torch.eye(tokens, dtype=torch.bool, device=h.device)[None, :, :]
    87	            valid_pairs = valid_pairs & ~eye
    88	            distance = distance.masked_fill(~valid_pairs, torch.inf)
    89	            neighbor_distance, neighbor_index = torch.topk(
    90	                distance, k=k, dim=-1, largest=False
    91	            )
    92	            h_all = h[:, None, :, :].expand(batch, tokens, tokens, dim)
    93	            gather_index = neighbor_index[..., None].expand(batch, tokens, k, dim)
    94	            neighbor = torch.gather(h_all, 2, gather_index)
    95	            center = h[:, :, None, :].expand_as(neighbor)
    96	            message = self.edge_mlp(torch.cat((center, neighbor - center), dim=-1))
    97	            neighbor_valid = torch.isfinite(neighbor_distance)
    98	            message = message.masked_fill(~neighbor_valid[..., None], -torch.inf)
    99	            aggregate = message.max(dim=2).values
   100	            aggregate = torch.where(
   101	                neighbor_valid.any(dim=2, keepdim=True),
   102	                aggregate,
   103	                torch.zeros_like(aggregate),
   104	            )
   105	            return self.norm(h + aggregate) * mask[..., None]

   108	    class CompactPET2Classifier(nn.Module):
   109	        """Point-edge encoder plus masked attention pooling and one logit."""
   110	
   111	        def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig):
   112	            super().__init__()
   113	            self.config = config.validated()
   114	            dim = config.hidden_dim
   115	            self.input_projection = nn.Sequential(
   116	                nn.Linear(config.continuous_dim, dim),
   117	                nn.GELU(),
   118	                nn.Linear(dim, dim),
   119	            )
   120	            # ID 0 is a fixed padding row.  Every real category is >=1.
   121	            self.type_embedding = nn.Embedding(
   122	                config.max_type_id + 1, dim, padding_idx=0
   123	            )
   124	            self.view_embedding = nn.Embedding(
   125	                config.max_view_id + 1, dim, padding_idx=0
   126	            )
   127	            self.edge_blocks = nn.ModuleList(
   128	                [_EdgeBlock(dim, config.k_neighbors) for _ in range(config.edge_layers)]
   129	            )
   130	            layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
   131	                d_model=dim,
   132	                nhead=config.num_heads,
   133	                dim_feedforward=2 * dim,
   134	                dropout=config.dropout,
   135	                activation="gelu",
   136	                batch_first=True,
   137	                norm_first=True,
   138	            )
   139	            self.transformer = nn.TransformerEncoder(
   140	                layer, num_layers=config.transformer_layers
   141	            )
   142	            self.global_projection = nn.Sequential(
   143	                nn.Linear(config.global_dim, dim),
   144	                nn.GELU(),
   145	                nn.Linear(dim, dim),
   146	            )
   147	            self.class_token = nn.Parameter(
   148	                torch.zeros(1, config.num_readout_tokens, dim)
   149	            )
   150	            self.output = nn.Sequential(
   151	                nn.LayerNorm(dim),
   152	                nn.Linear(dim, dim),
   153	                nn.GELU(),
   154	                nn.Linear(dim, 1),
   155	            )
   156	            nn.init.normal_(self.class_token, std=0.02)
   157	
   158	        def forward(
   159	            self,
   160	            continuous,
   161	            coords,
   162	            token_mask,
   163	            type_id,
   164	            view_id,
   165	            globals_,
   166	        ):
   167	            if token_mask.dtype is not torch.bool:
   168	                raise TypeError("token_mask must be torch.bool")
   169	            if torch.any(type_id[token_mask] == 0):
   170	                raise ValueError("real tokens cannot use category 0")
   171	            if torch.any(type_id[~token_mask] != 0):
   172	                raise ValueError("padded tokens must use type category 0")
   173	            h = (
   174	                self.input_projection(continuous)
   175	                + self.type_embedding(type_id)
   176	                + self.view_embedding(view_id)
   177	            )
   178	            h = h * token_mask[..., None]
   179	            for block in self.edge_blocks:
   180	                h = block(h, coords, token_mask)
   181	            readout_tokens = self.class_token.expand(h.shape[0], -1, -1)
   182	            readout_tokens = readout_tokens + self.global_projection(globals_)[:, None, :]
   183	            sequence = torch.cat((readout_tokens, h), dim=1)
   184	            class_mask = torch.zeros(
   185	                (h.shape[0], self.config.num_readout_tokens),
   186	                dtype=torch.bool,
   187	                device=h.device,
   188	            )
   189	            padding_mask = torch.cat((class_mask, ~token_mask), dim=1)
   190	            encoded = self.transformer(
   191	                sequence, src_key_padding_mask=padding_mask
   192	            )
   193	            pooled = encoded[:, : self.config.num_readout_tokens].mean(dim=1)
   194	            return self.output(pooled).squeeze(-1)

   216	def concatenate_batches(parts: Sequence[TokenBatch], provenance: str) -> TokenBatch:
   217	    if not parts:
   218	        raise ValueError("cannot concatenate an empty batch sequence")
   219	    checked = [part.validated() for part in parts]
   220	    reference = checked[0]
   221	    fields = ("continuous", "coords", "token_mask", "type_id", "view_id", "globals")
   222	    for part in checked[1:]:
   223	        if part.continuous.shape[1:] != reference.continuous.shape[1:]:
   224	            raise ValueError("token continuous schemas differ")
   225	        if part.coords.shape[1:] != reference.coords.shape[1:]:
   226	            raise ValueError("coordinate schemas differ")
   227	        if part.global_names != reference.global_names:
   228	            raise ValueError("global schemas differ")
   229	        if (part.muon_present is None) != (reference.muon_present is None):
   230	            raise ValueError("muon token seams differ")
   231	    kwargs = {name: np.concatenate([getattr(p, name) for p in checked]) for name in fields}
   232	    kwargs["row_index"] = np.arange(sum(p.n_rows for p in checked), dtype=np.int64)
   233	    kwargs["global_names"] = reference.global_names
   234	    kwargs["provenance"] = provenance
   235	    for name in ("overflow_energy", "muon_continuous", "muon_coords", "muon_present"):
   236	        values = [getattr(p, name) for p in checked]
   237	        kwargs[name] = None if values[0] is None else np.concatenate(values)

   111	def _ratio_metrics(
   112	    fixture,
   113	    predicted: np.ndarray,
   114	    expected: np.ndarray,
   115	    *,
   116	    step: str,
   117	) -> dict:
   118	    signal = fixture.dataset.signal
   119	    predicted = np.asarray(predicted, dtype=np.float64)
   120	    expected = np.asarray(expected, dtype=np.float64)
   121	    if predicted.shape != expected.shape or predicted.shape != (signal.reco.n_rows,):
   122	        raise ValueError("conditional stress ratio arrays are not full-order")
   123	    valid = signal.pass_reco if step == "pull" else signal.pass_truth
   124	    base = (
   125	        fixture.dataset.pot_scale
   126	        * (signal.w_reco if step == "pull" else signal.w_truth)
   127	    )
   128	    residual = np.log(predicted[valid]) - np.log(expected[valid])
   129	    expected_weight = base[valid] * expected[valid]
   130	    predicted_weight = base[valid] * predicted[valid]
   131	    paired = fixture.pair_rows.reshape(-1)
   132	    paired = paired[valid[paired]]
   133	    hidden = fixture.hidden_sign[paired]
   134	    group = {}
   135	    for sign in (-1, 1):
   136	        rows = paired[hidden == sign]
   137	        group[str(sign)] = {
   138	            "count": int(len(rows)),
   139	            "expected_ratio_mean": float(np.mean(expected[rows])),
   140	            "predicted_ratio_mean": float(np.mean(predicted[rows])),
   141	            "predicted_ratio_std": float(np.std(predicted[rows])),
   142	        }
   143	    tail = fixture.declared_tail_mask & valid
   144	    return {
   145	        "step": step,
   146	        "row_count": int(valid.sum()),
   147	        "log_ratio_residual": {
   148	            "bias": float(np.mean(residual)),
   149	            "mae": float(np.mean(np.abs(residual))),
   150	            "rmse": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(residual)))),
   151	            "quantiles": np.quantile(
   152	                residual, [0.0, 0.01, 0.5, 0.99, 1.0]
   153	            ).tolist(),
   154	        },
   155	        "expected_ratio": weight_summary(expected[valid]),
   156	        "predicted_ratio": weight_summary(predicted[valid]),
   157	        "expected_weight": weight_summary(expected_weight),
   158	        "predicted_weight": weight_summary(predicted_weight),
   159	        "ess": {
   160	            "global_expected": effective_sample_size(expected_weight),
   161	            "global_predicted": effective_sample_size(predicted_weight),
   162	            "tail_expected": effective_sample_size(base[tail] * expected[tail]),
   163	            "tail_predicted": effective_sample_size(base[tail] * predicted[tail]),
   164	            "tail_count": int(tail.sum()),
   165	        },
   166	        "hidden_sign_groups": group,
   167	        "full_order": bool(
   168	            np.array_equal(signal.reco.row_index, np.arange(signal.reco.n_rows))
   169	        ),
   170	    }

    33	def _cap_telemetry(iterations: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, float | int]:
    34	    counts = {10: 0, 30: 0}
    35	    weight_masses = {10: 0.0, 30: 0.0}
    36	    shifts = []
    37	    for iteration in iterations:
    38	        for step in ("step1_inference", "step2_inference"):
    39	            inference = iteration[step]
    40	            sensitivity = inference["cap_sensitivity"]
    41	            cap10 = sensitivity["cap_10"]
    42	            cap30 = sensitivity["cap_30"]
    43	            counts[10] += int(cap10["saturated_count"])
    44	            counts[30] += int(cap30["saturated_count"])
    45	            weight_masses[10] += float(
    46	                cap10["saturated_reference_weight_mass"]
    47	            )
    48	            weight_masses[30] += float(
    49	                cap30["saturated_reference_weight_mass"]
    50	            )
    51	            ess10 = float(cap10["reweighted_ess"])
    52	            ess30 = float(cap30["reweighted_ess"])
    53	            shifts.append(abs(ess10 - ess30) / max(abs(ess30), 1e-12))
    54	    return {
    55	        "cap10_saturated_count": counts[10],
    56	        "cap30_saturated_count": counts[30],
    57	        "cap10_saturated_reference_weight_mass": weight_masses[10],
    58	        "cap30_saturated_reference_weight_mass": weight_masses[30],
    59	        "cap10_vs_cap30_max_relative_ess_shift": float(
    60	            max(shifts, default=0.0)
    61	        ),
    62	    }

    13	def _quantile_edges(values: np.ndarray, bins: int) -> np.ndarray:
    14	    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)
    15	    edges = np.unique(np.quantile(values, np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, bins + 1)))
    16	    if edges.size < 2:
    17	        center = float(values[0])
    18	        edges = np.asarray([center - 0.5, center + 0.5])
    19	    edges[0] = np.nextafter(edges[0], -np.inf)
    20	    edges[-1] = np.nextafter(edges[-1], np.inf)
    21	    return edges

    24	def _projection_residual(
    25	    coordinates: np.ndarray,
    26	    expected_weights: np.ndarray,
    27	    predicted_weights: np.ndarray,
    28	    bins_per_axis: int,
    29	) -> dict[str, Any]:
    30	    coordinates = np.asarray(coordinates, dtype=np.float64)
    31	    edges = [
    32	        _quantile_edges(coordinates[:, column], bins_per_axis)
    33	        for column in range(coordinates.shape[1])
    34	    ]
    35	    expected = np.histogramdd(coordinates, bins=edges, weights=expected_weights)[0]
    36	    predicted = np.histogramdd(coordinates, bins=edges, weights=predicted_weights)[0]
    37	    residual = predicted - expected
    38	    expected_mass = float(expected.sum())
    39	    denom = np.maximum(expected, 1e-12)
    40	    occupied = (expected > 0) | (predicted > 0)
    41	    return {
    42	        "dimensions": int(coordinates.shape[1]),
    43	        "shape": list(expected.shape),
    44	        "expected_mass": expected_mass,
    45	        "predicted_mass": float(predicted.sum()),
    46	        "relative_l1": float(np.abs(residual).sum() / max(expected_mass, 1e-12)),
    47	        "occupied_bin_rms_fractional": float(
    48	            np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(residual[occupied] / denom[occupied])))
    49	        ),
    50	        "max_abs_fractional": float(
    51	            np.max(np.abs(residual[occupied]) / denom[occupied])
    52	        ),
    53	    }

    19	def atomic_run_directory(path: os.PathLike[str] | str) -> Iterator[Path]:
    20	    """Create a complete run in a sibling temp directory, then atomically publish it."""
    21	    destination = Path(path).resolve()
    22	    if destination.exists():
    23	        raise FileExistsError(f"refusing to overwrite existing run directory: {destination}")
    24	    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    25	    temporary = Path(
    26	        tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f".{destination.name}.tmp-", dir=destination.parent)
    27	    )
    28	    try:
    29	        yield temporary
    30	        os.replace(temporary, destination)
    31	    except Exception:
    32	        shutil.rmtree(temporary, ignore_errors=True)
    33	        raise

    36	def write_json(path: os.PathLike[str] | str, payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    37	    path = Path(path)
    38	    temporary = path.with_name(f".{path.name}.tmp-{os.getpid()}")
    39	    temporary.write_text(canonical_json(payload) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    40	    os.replace(temporary, path)

    45	    fd, temporary_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
    46	        prefix=f".{path.name}.tmp-", suffix=".npz", dir=path.parent
    47	    )
    48	    os.close(fd)
    49	    try:
    50	        np.savez_compressed(temporary_name, **arrays)
    51	        os.replace(temporary_name, path)
    52	    finally:

   110	def _write_packet(path: Path, arrays=None):
   111	    np.savez_compressed(path, **(_tiny_g2_arrays() if arrays is None else arrays))
   112	    return file_sha256(path), path.stat().st_size

   115	def _rewrite_member(path: Path, key: str, transform):
   116	    member = f"{key}.npy"
   117	    with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "r") as archive:
   118	        payloads = {
   119	            info.filename: archive.read(info.filename)
   120	            for info in archive.infolist()
   121	        }
   122	    payloads[member] = transform(payloads[member])
   123	    replacement = path.with_suffix(".replacement.npz")
   124	    with zipfile.ZipFile(
   125	        replacement, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
   126	    ) as archive:
   127	        for name, payload in payloads.items():
   128	            archive.writestr(name, payload)
   129	    replacement.replace(path)
   130	    return file_sha256(path), path.stat().st_size

   350	        and source_header == expected_header

   355	def _streaming_array_hash(
   356	    arrays: tuple[np.ndarray, ...], *, chunk_bytes: int = DEFAULT_CHUNK_BYTES
   357	) -> str:
   358	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
   359	    for value in arrays:
   360	        array = np.asarray(value)
   361	        if not array.flags.c_contiguous:
   362	            raise ValueError("legacy inventory hash requires C-contiguous arrays")
   363	        # Match g2_adapter._legacy_order_hash byte-for-byte.  The frozen G2
   364	        # producer used str(dtype), not NumPy's endian-explicit dtype.str.
   365	        digest.update(str(array.dtype).encode())
   366	        digest.update(repr(array.shape).encode())
   367	        raw = array.view(np.uint8).reshape(-1)
   368	        for start in range(0, raw.size, chunk_bytes):
   369	            digest.update(memoryview(raw[start : start + chunk_bytes]))
   370	    return digest.hexdigest()

   373	def _row_counts(arrays: Mapping[str, np.ndarray]) -> dict[str, int]:
   374	    result: dict[str, int] = {}
   375	    for family, keys in ROW_FAMILY_KEYS.items():
   376	        counts = {int(arrays[key].shape[0]) for key in keys}
   377	        if len(counts) != 1:
   378	            raise ValueError(f"{family} array row counts disagree: {sorted(counts)}")
   379	        result[family] = counts.pop()
   380	    return result

   403	@dataclass
   404	class G2MemmapInventory:
   405	    root: Path
   406	    manifest: Mapping[str, Any]
   407	    arrays: Mapping[str, np.ndarray]
   408	
   409	    @property
   410	    def row_counts(self) -> Mapping[str, int]:
   411	        return self.manifest["row_counts"]
   412	
   413	    def window(self, family: str, start: int, stop: int) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
   414	        if family not in ROW_FAMILY_KEYS:
   415	            raise ValueError(f"unknown row family: {family}")
   416	        count = int(self.row_counts[family])
   417	        if not (0 <= start <= stop <= count):
   418	            raise ValueError(f"invalid {family} window [{start},{stop}) for {count} rows")
   419	        return {key: self.arrays[key][start:stop] for key in ROW_FAMILY_KEYS[family]}
   420	
   421	    def iter_windows(
   422	        self, family: str, chunk_rows: int
   423	    ) -> Iterator[tuple[int, int, dict[str, np.ndarray]]]:
   424	        if chunk_rows < 1:
   425	            raise ValueError("chunk_rows must be positive")
   426	        count = int(self.row_counts[family])
   427	        for start in range(0, count, chunk_rows):
   428	            stop = min(count, start + chunk_rows)
   429	            yield start, stop, self.window(family, start, stop)
   430	
   431	    def close(self) -> None:
   432	        for value in self.arrays.values():
   433	            mmap = getattr(value, "_mmap", None)
   434	            if mmap is not None:
   435	                mmap.close()

   438	def open_g2_memmap_inventory(
   439	    directory: str | Path,
   440	    *,
   441	    source_npz: str | Path,
   442	    verify_hashes: bool = True,
   443	    chunk_bytes: int = DEFAULT_CHUNK_BYTES,
   444	) -> G2MemmapInventory:
   445	    root = Path(directory).expanduser().resolve()
   446	    manifest_path = root / MANIFEST_NAME
   447	    complete_path = root / COMPLETE_NAME
   448	    if not root.is_dir() or not manifest_path.is_file() or not complete_path.is_file():
   449	        raise FileNotFoundError("G2 memmap inventory is partial or lacks completion markers")
   450	    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   451	    complete = json.loads(complete_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   452	    if manifest.get("format_version") != FORMAT_VERSION:
   453	        raise ValueError("wrong G2 memmap format version")
   454	    if complete.get("format_version") != FORMAT_VERSION:
   455	        raise ValueError("wrong G2 completion-marker format version")
   456	    if complete.get("manifest_sha256") != file_sha256(manifest_path):
   457	        raise ValueError("G2 completion marker does not bind the manifest")
   458	    if complete.get("input_sha256") != manifest.get("input", {}).get("sha256"):
   459	        raise ValueError("G2 completion marker does not bind the input receipt")
   460	    if (
   461	        manifest.get("status") != "complete_code_contract_only"
   462	        or manifest.get("evidence_class") != "code-contract"
   463	        or manifest.get("g2_validation_claim") is not False
   464	        or manifest.get("publication_promotion_permitted") is not False
   465	    ):
   466	        raise ValueError("G2 manifest carries an invalid evidence status")
   467	    source = Path(source_npz).expanduser().resolve()
   468	    if (
   469	        not source.is_file()
   470	        or source.stat().st_size != int(manifest["input"]["size_bytes"])
   471	        or file_sha256(source, chunk_bytes=chunk_bytes)
   472	        != manifest["input"]["sha256"]
   473	    ):
   474	        raise ValueError("G2 source is stale, absent, or disagrees with the manifest")
   475	    arrays: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
   476	    records = manifest.get("arrays", {})
   477	    if set(records) != set(REQUIRED_G2_KEYS):
   478	        raise ValueError("G2 manifest array inventory is incomplete")
   479	    try:
   480	        for key in sorted(REQUIRED_G2_KEYS):
   481	            record = records[key]
   482	            if (
   483	                record.get("name") != key
   484	                or record.get("path") != f"{key}.npy"
   485	                or record.get("row_family") != KEY_TO_FAMILY.get(key, "metadata")
   486	                or record.get("units") != ARRAY_UNITS[key]
   487	            ):
   488	                raise ValueError(f"G2 manifest record semantics mismatch for {key}")
   489	            path = root / record["path"]
   490	            if not path.is_file():
   491	                raise FileNotFoundError(f"G2 memmap array is absent: {key}")
   492	            if verify_hashes and file_sha256(path, chunk_bytes=chunk_bytes) != record["sha256"]:
   493	                raise ValueError(f"G2 memmap array content hash mismatch: {key}")
   494	            value = np.load(path, mmap_mode="r", allow_pickle=False)
   495	            if not isinstance(value, np.memmap):
   496	                raise ValueError(f"G2 array is not memmap-backed: {key}")
   497	            if value.flags.writeable:
   498	                raise ValueError(f"G2 memmap unexpectedly opened writable: {key}")
   499	            with path.open("rb") as handle:
   500	                header_shape, header_fortran, header_dtype = _read_member_header(
   501	                    handle
   502	                )
   503	            actual = {
   504	                "dtype": header_dtype.str,
   505	                "shape": list(header_shape),
   506	                "fortran_order": header_fortran,
   507	            }
   508	            expected = {
   509	                name: record[name] for name in ("dtype", "shape", "fortran_order")
   510	            }
   511	            if actual != expected:
   512	                raise ValueError(f"G2 memmap schema mismatch for {key}")
   513	            arrays[key] = value
   514	        counts = _row_counts(arrays)
   515	        if counts != {key: int(value) for key, value in manifest["row_counts"].items()}:
   516	            raise ValueError("G2 row-family counts disagree with the manifest")
   517	        identities = _identity_hashes(arrays, chunk_bytes=chunk_bytes)
   518	        if identities != manifest["identity_hashes"]:
   519	            raise ValueError("G2 ordered-inventory hashes disagree with the manifest")
   520	        for key, computed in identities.items():
   521	            if _scalar_text(arrays[key]) != computed:
   522	                raise ValueError(f"G2 embedded ordered-inventory hash disagrees: {key}")
   523	    except Exception:
   524	        for value in arrays.values():
   525	            mmap = getattr(value, "_mmap", None)
   526	            if mmap is not None:
   527	                mmap.close()
   528	        raise
   529	    return G2MemmapInventory(root=root, manifest=manifest, arrays=arrays)

   682	            "publication_promotion_permitted": False,

   688	            },
   689	            "schema_markers": preflight["markers"],
   690	            "arrays": progress["arrays"],
   691	            "row_counts": counts,
   692	            "identity_hashes": identities,
   693	            "chunk_bytes": chunk_bytes,

   113	def _raw_objects(
   114	    rng: np.random.Generator,
   115	    n: int,
   116	    raw_tokens: int,
   117	    latent: np.ndarray,
   118	    conditional_shift: float = 0.0,
   119	):
   120	    count = rng.integers(2, raw_tokens + 1, size=n)
   121	    object_mask = np.arange(raw_tokens)[None, :] < count[:, None]
   122	    base = np.exp(
   123	        0.25 * latent[:, None]
   124	        + rng.normal(0.0, 0.45, size=(n, raw_tokens))
   125	        + conditional_shift * (latent[:, None] > 0)
   126	    )
   127	    continuous = np.zeros((n, raw_tokens, 4), dtype=np.float32)
   128	    continuous[:, :, 0] = base
   129	    continuous[:, :, 1] = rng.normal(latent[:, None], 0.7, size=(n, raw_tokens))
   130	    continuous[:, :, 2] = rng.normal(0.4 * latent[:, None], 0.8, size=(n, raw_tokens))
   131	    continuous[:, :, 3] = rng.normal(0.0, 0.25, size=(n, raw_tokens))
   132	    continuous[~object_mask] = 0.0
   133	    type_id = rng.choice(
   134	        np.asarray([TYPE_RECO_CLUSTER, TYPE_TRACK]),
   135	        size=(n, raw_tokens),
   136	        p=[0.7, 0.3],
   137	    ).astype(np.int64)
   138	    view_id = rng.integers(1, 4, size=(n, raw_tokens), dtype=np.int64)
   139	    type_id[~object_mask] = 0
   140	    view_id[~object_mask] = 0
   141	    return continuous, type_id, view_id, object_mask
   142

   144	def _globals(rng, latent, distortion=0.0):
   145	    mu_pt = np.exp(0.15 * latent + distortion * (latent > 0))
   146	    mu_pparallel = 3.0 + 0.5 * latent + rng.normal(0, 0.1, len(latent))
   147	    mu_energy = np.sqrt(np.square(mu_pt) + np.square(mu_pparallel) + 0.105**2)
   148	    mu_phi = rng.uniform(-np.pi, np.pi, len(latent))
   149	    eavail = np.exp(0.3 * latent + rng.normal(0, 0.15, len(latent)))
   150	    q3 = np.sqrt(np.square(mu_pt) + np.square(eavail))
   151	    charge = np.where(rng.random(len(latent)) > 0.05, -1.0, 1.0)
   152	    minos = np.ones(len(latent))
   153	    vertex = rng.normal(0, 0.3, size=(len(latent), 3))
   154	    return np.column_stack(
   155	        (
   156	            mu_pt,
   157	            mu_pparallel,
   158	            mu_energy,
   159	            np.cos(mu_phi),
   160	            np.sin(mu_phi),
   161	            eavail,
   162	            q3,
   163	            charge,
   164	            minos,
   165	            vertex,
   166	        )
   167	    ).astype(np.float32)

   170	def _batch(
   171	    rng,
   172	    latent,
   173	    max_tokens,
   174	    provenance,
   175	    *,
   176	    distortion=0.0,
   177	    valid_rows=None,
   178	):
   179	    n = len(latent)
   180	    raw = _raw_objects(rng, n, max_tokens + 4, latent, distortion)
   181	    continuous, type_id, view_id, mask, overflow = truncate_with_overflow(
   182	        *raw, max_tokens=max_tokens
   183	    )
   184	    globals_ = _globals(rng, latent, distortion)
   185	    muon = np.zeros((n, continuous.shape[2]), dtype=np.float32)
   186	    muon[:, 0] = globals_[:, 2]
   187	    muon[:, 1] = globals_[:, 0]
   188	    muon[:, 2] = globals_[:, 1]
   189	    muon[:, 3] = np.arctan2(globals_[:, 4], globals_[:, 3])
   190	    muon_present = np.ones(n, dtype=bool)
   191	    if valid_rows is not None:
   192	        valid_rows = np.asarray(valid_rows, bool)
   193	        continuous[~valid_rows] = 0.0
   194	        type_id[~valid_rows] = 0
   195	        view_id[~valid_rows] = 0
   196	        mask[~valid_rows] = False
   197	        globals_[~valid_rows] = 0.0
   198	        muon[~valid_rows] = 0.0
   199	        muon_present = valid_rows.copy()
   200	        overflow[~valid_rows] = 0.0
   201	    return TokenBatch(
   202	        continuous=continuous,
   203	        coords=continuous[:, :, 1:3].copy(),
   204	        token_mask=mask,
   205	        type_id=type_id,
   206	        view_id=view_id,
   207	        globals=globals_,
   208	        row_index=np.arange(n, dtype=np.int64),
   209	        global_names=GLOBAL_NAMES,
   210	        provenance=provenance,
   211	        overflow_energy=overflow,
   212	        muon_continuous=muon,
   213	        # Synthetic detector-plane coordinates are generated with the same
   214	        # event vertex and are explicitly fixture-only evidence.
   215	        muon_coords=globals_[:, [9, 11]].copy(),
   216	        muon_present=muon_present,
   217	    ).validated(max_type=TYPE_OVERFLOW, max_view=VIEW_AGGREGATE)

   229	        raise ValueError("fixture inventories must each contain at least eight rows")

   231	    latent_truth = rng.normal(size=n_signal)
   232	    pass_truth = np.ones(n_signal, dtype=bool)
   233	    pass_truth[: max(1, n_signal // 50)] = False
   234	    reco_probability = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-(0.3 + 0.6 * latent_truth)))
   235	    pass_reco = (rng.random(n_signal) < reco_probability) & pass_truth

   237	    pass_reco[pass_truth] = pass_reco[pass_truth]

   240	    pass_reco[truth_indices[1]] = False
   241	    latent_reco = latent_truth + rng.normal(0.0, 0.25, n_signal)

   243	        rng,
   244	        latent_reco,
   245	        max_tokens,
   246	        "synthetic_signal_reco",
   247	        valid_rows=pass_reco,
   248	    )

   251	        latent_truth,
   252	        max_tokens,

   254	        valid_rows=pass_truth,
   255	    )
   256	    latent_data = rng.normal(0.25, 1.0, n_data)
   257	    # Conditional shift is deliberately not a one-dimensional marginal tilt.
   258	    data = _batch(
   259	        rng,
   260	        latent_data,
   261	        max_tokens,
   262	        "synthetic_data_conditional_distortion",
   263	        distortion=0.32,
   264	    )
   265	    latent_bkg = rng.normal(-0.8, 1.2, n_background)
   266	    background = _batch(
   267	        rng,
   268	        latent_bkg,
   269	        max_tokens,
   270	        "synthetic_literal_background",
   271	        distortion=-0.12,
   272	    )

   314	                "negative_weight_provenance_retained": True,
   315	                "not_publication_gate2": True,

   318	        ),

   320	        schema={

   328	            "overflow": "pre-truncation energy-conserving aggregate",

   352	def make_known_ratio_closure_dataset(
   353	    n_signal: int = 256,
   354	    n_background: int = 40,
   355	    max_tokens: int = 7,
   356	    seed: int = 424242,
   357	) -> ConditionalClosureFixture:
   358	    """Build aligned pseudo-data with a known conditional event-weight ratio.
   359	
   360	    Pseudo-data rows are exact copies of selected simulated reco rows.  Their
   361	    nonnegative target mass is ``w_reco * r(reco)`` with an analytic ratio that
   362	    depends jointly on muon and recoil observables.  Literal backgrounds remain
   363	    present with signed negative provenance but zero Stay-Positive training
   364	    mass, so they cannot alter the known target measure.
   365	    """
   366	    dataset, capabilities = make_synthetic_dataset(
   367	        n_signal=n_signal,
   368	        n_data=max(16, n_signal // 2),
   369	        n_background=n_background,
   370	        max_tokens=max_tokens,
   371	        seed=seed,
   372	    )
   373	    signal = dataset.signal
   374	    selected = np.flatnonzero(signal.pass_reco)
   375	    if selected.size < 12:
   376	        raise ValueError("known-ratio fixture requires at least twelve selected reco rows")
   377	    reco = signal.reco
   378	    token_energy = np.sum(
   379	        np.where(reco.token_mask, reco.continuous[:, :, 0], 0.0), axis=1
   380	    )
   380	    )
   381	    mu_pt = reco.globals[:, reco.global_names.index("mu_pt")]
   382	    selected_energy = np.log1p(token_energy[selected])
   383	    selected_mu = np.log(np.maximum(mu_pt[selected], 1e-8))
   384	    z_energy = (selected_energy - selected_energy.mean()) / max(
   385	        float(selected_energy.std()), 1e-8
   386	    )
   387	    z_mu = (selected_mu - selected_mu.mean()) / max(float(selected_mu.std()), 1e-8)
   388	    log_ratio = 0.42 * z_mu + 0.38 * z_mu * np.tanh(z_energy)
   389	    analytic_ratio = np.exp(np.clip(log_ratio, -2.0, 2.0))
   390	    # Unit weighted mean removes an overall normalization tilt while preserving
   391	    # the conditional shape.  Uneven MC event masses remain explicit.
   392	    analytic_ratio /= np.average(analytic_ratio, weights=signal.w_reco[selected])
   393	
   394	    data = signal.reco.subset(selected)
   395	    data = replace(
   396	        data,
   397	        row_index=np.arange(selected.size, dtype=np.int64),
   398	        provenance="synthetic_aligned_known_ratio_pseudodata",
   399	    ).validated()
   400	    background = dataset.measured.background
   401	    data_weights = signal.w_reco[selected] * analytic_ratio
   402	    background_abs = np.abs(
   403	        dataset.measured.raw_signed_weights[-background.n_rows :]
   404	    )
   405	    refined = np.concatenate(
   406	        (data_weights.astype(np.float64), np.zeros(background.n_rows, dtype=np.float64))
   407	    )
   408	    raw_signed = np.concatenate((data_weights, -background_abs))
   409	    measured = MeasuredInventory(
   410	        data=data,
   411	        background=background,
   412	        refined_weights=refined,
   413	        raw_signed_weights=raw_signed,
   414	        data_identity_hash="",
   415	        background_identity_hash="",
   416	        target_receipt={
   417	            "kind": "synthetic_aligned_analytic_ratio_v1",
   418	            "canonical_nonnegative": True,
   419	            "ordering": "aligned_data_then_literal_background",
   420	            "negative_weight_provenance_retained": True,
   421	            "background_refined_training_mass": 0.0,
   422	            "analytic_formula": (
   423	                "exp(0.42*z(log(mu_pt)) + "
   424	                "0.38*z(log(mu_pt))*tanh(z(log1p(token_energy))))"
   425	            ),
   426	            "normalization": "w_reco-weighted selected-event mean ratio equals one",
   427	            "seed": seed,
   428	            "not_publication_gate2": True,
   429	        },
   430	        aligned_signal_row=np.concatenate(
   431	            (selected.astype(np.int64), -np.ones(background.n_rows, dtype=np.int64))
   432	        ),
   433	    ).validated()
   434	    expected = np.ones(n_signal, dtype=np.float64)
   435	    expected[selected] = analytic_ratio
   436	    q3_index = signal.truth.global_names.index("q3")
   437	    truth_valid = signal.pass_truth
   438	    tail_threshold = float(
   439	        np.quantile(signal.truth.globals[truth_valid, q3_index], 0.8)
   440	    )
   441	    tail = truth_valid & (signal.truth.globals[:, q3_index] >= tail_threshold)
   442	    closure_dataset = replace(
   443	        dataset,
   444	        measured=measured,
   445	        estimator_fingerprint="pet2-synthetic-known-ratio-closure-v1",
   446	        schema={
   447	            **dict(dataset.schema),
   448	            "source": "portable_synthetic_known_ratio_closure",
   449	            "pseudo_data_alignment": "exact selected signal reco rows",
   450	            "known_conditional_ratio": measured.target_receipt["analytic_formula"],
   451	            "background_training_role": (
   452	                "literal aligned rows retained; zero refined mass with signed provenance"
   453	            ),
   454	        },
   455	    ).validated()
   456	    return ConditionalClosureFixture(
   457	        dataset=closure_dataset,
   458	        capabilities=capabilities,
   459	        data_to_signal_row=selected.astype(np.int64),
   460	        analytic_reco_ratio=analytic_ratio.astype(np.float64),
   461	        expected_truth_ratio=expected,
   462	        declared_tail_mask=tail,
   463	        specification={
   464	            "evidence_class": "portable_synthetic_known_ratio",
   465	            "fixture_seed": seed,
   466	            "selected_rows": int(selected.size),
   467	            "native_misses": int(np.sum(signal.pass_truth & ~signal.pass_reco)),
   468	            "ratio_quantiles": np.quantile(

   470	            ).tolist(),
   471	            "tail_definition": {
   472	                "feature": "truth_q3",
   473	                "quantile": 0.8,
   474	                "threshold": tail_threshold,
   475	                "count": int(tail.sum()),
   476	            },
   477	            "g2_validation_claim": False,
   478	        },
   479	    )

   482	def analytic_gaussian_problem(
   483	    points: np.ndarray,
   484	    *,
   485	    mean0: float = -0.5,
   486	    mean1: float = 0.75,
   487	    sigma: float = 1.2,
   488	    mass0: float = 3.0,
   489	    mass1: float = 11.0,
   490	) -> dict[str, Any]:
   491	    """Known balanced logit and physical ratio for unequal weighted masses."""
   492	    x = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float64)
   493	    log_p1_over_p0 = (
   494	        -0.5 * np.square((x - mean1) / sigma)
   495	        + 0.5 * np.square((x - mean0) / sigma)
   496	    )
   497	    physical_ratio = np.exp(log_p1_over_p0) * mass1 / mass0
   498	    return {
   499	        "points": x,
   500	        "balanced_logit": log_p1_over_p0,
   501	        "physical_ratio": physical_ratio,
   502	        "mass0": mass0,
   503	        "mass1": mass1,
   504	    }

I also found a weaker defense-in-depth issue in resumable conversion (journal record semantics were not fully revalidated) and a real muon-KNN edge case: rows with too few recoil tokens could carry coordinates that the fixed K=3 graph could not distinguish. I’m repairing these with focused regressions.

item.text: The first repair pass is in place. The fixture now guarantees six recoil tokens around the additive muon token, so this model’s fixed K=3 edge block sees different complete neighborhoods rather than merely different coordinates; the certificate computes that relationship. The converter now has no hash-disable option, fingerprints its progress journal and manifest, revalidates resumed records, and rebinds the source immediately before publication.

# Experimental native PyTorch PET2-family backend

Status: independent, opt-in, synthetic/diagnostic only. It does not replace or
modify any TensorFlow/Keras, recoil-only, GBDT, ROOT, or publication default.

## Contract

- Explicit boolean token masks; continuous features never define padding.
- Category `0` is pad/unknown only; real types begin at `1`.
- Step 1 uses detector-observable reco/data/literal-background fields only.
- `w_reco` and `w_truth` remain separate.
- Negative background provenance remains signed audit metadata. Only the
  receipt-bound nonnegative Stay-Positive target reaches training.
- Truth-only misses skip Step 1, retain their incoming push, and enter Step 2.
- Balanced weighted BCE is calibrated by `log(W1/W0)` before the log-ratio cap.
- Full-order inference requires `mc_indices == arange(N)`.
- Every arm, preprocessing recipe, split, input, and output is fingerprinted.

The comparison arms are deliberately split:

- `C`: generic tokens on the TF-B-matched numeric footing, including the
  baseline reconstructed `(mu_pt, mu_pparallel)` summaries but no
  view/type/rich-global feature.
- `D-view`: C plus the separate detector-view category.
- `D-typed`: C plus real reconstructed object types, only when supplied.
- `E-muon`: C plus the remaining audited reconstructed-muon object globals
  `(energy, cos(phi), sin(phi))`.
- `E-rich-no-charge`: E-muon plus audited eavail/q3/MINOS/vertex globals.
- `E-rich`: E-rich-no-charge plus audited charge (unavailable for G2).
- `F`: unavailable until a strict manifest proves checksum, weight license,
  architecture, preprocessing, and tensor compatibility.

Every random arm uses the same fixed superset input tensors and parameter
shapes; disabled features are zero-masked. Overflow is a separate declared
switch. Muon-token mode is synthetic-only because G2 has no audited physical
KNN coordinate convention.

The reco arm is applied only to Step 1. Step 2 always uses the same
`truth-frozen` manifest: generic tokens, no detector view, no overflow/muon
token, and only the separately normalized truth-muon pT/p-parallel globals.
This prevents a reco view/type/rich-global ablation from silently changing the
truth density-ratio problem or manufacturing MINOS/vertex counterparts.

The default C/D/E capacity is the independently implemented PET2-small concept
profile established by the source audit: hidden dimension 128, eight attention
heads, eight transformer blocks, and four readout tokens. It is a conceptual
architecture match, not copied source or checkpoint compatibility. Tests may
request a smaller explicit profile for portable CPU execution.

The G2 adapter fails closed because the publication G2 and Gate-2 payload are
not included locally. It is explicitly a compressed-NPZ **mini-packet** seam:
it reads NPY headers first and rejects production-sized/40--50M-row NPZ before
`np.load`. It does not advertise eager full-G2 loading. G2 detector view is
not treated as object type, and no photon/blob/prong/dE/dx labels are invented.
The absent-G2 unit assumptions are recorded in every adapted dataset: point
clouds/muons/vertices are assumed MeV/mm and scalar kinematics already GeV,
matching the audited producer contract but not independently rechecked against
the locally absent minerva-ml payload. SHA binding is load-time evidence, not
a substitute for that absent-data validation.

The `/1000` error in the Gate-2 validator's independent scalar histogram was
corrected in source and covered by login-safe regressions. The historical
independent receipt has **not** been rerun and is not upgraded by this change.

G2 POT normalization is carried in the dataset contract from the Gate-2
receipt. An engine caller must explicitly repeat exactly that scale; unset or
different G2 values fail before training. Portable synthetic fixtures carry an
explicit scale of 1.

## Evidence fixtures

`make_known_ratio_closure_dataset` copies selected simulated reco rows into
pseudo-data and assigns the analytic event mass `w_reco * r(reco)`. It provides
known event-level reco/truth targets, native misses, signed literal background
provenance, full-iteration closure metrics, cap count/mass, global/tail ESS,
and two-dimensional and three-dimensional projection residuals. The CLI emits
per-arm/per-seed JSON. The frozen matched recipe is:

```text
fixture seed 424242; estimator seeds 101/202/303; split seed 424242;
70/15/15 split; two iterations; eight epochs/step; batch 512;
AdamW lr=1e-4, weight_decay=1e-2
```

Any override must use `--recipe smoke`, which records that comparison claims
are not permitted. `ratio_conventions.py` proves only the fixed-logit physical
ratio equivalence between TF posterior odds and balanced PyTorch logits plus
the class-mass offset; it makes no layer/training equivalence claim.

The completed known-ratio matrix is a baseline-sufficient null-feature test:
its ratio depends only on muon pT and total token energy, both visible to C.
`conditional_fixtures.py` supplies the separate continuation test. It builds
split-local counterfactual pairs whose materialized parent tensors are
byte-identical while exactly one enriched carrier—view, reconstructed type,
rich global, additive muon-token geometry, or overflow—encodes a fixed
0.5/1.5 target. Each family has signal, unity-sham, and carrier-shuffle modes
on one unchanged truth inventory. The muon fixture constructs two
three-recoil neighborhoods, so the model's fixed K=3 coordinate graph—not
just an external decoder—can express the carrier. This tests whether the
channel can transmit conditional information; it does not show that real
MINERvA data contains a beneficial conditional.

Login-safe contract example:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=nd-unfolding python3 -m pet2_torch.conditional_stress_cli \
  --out /tmp/pet2-conditional-contract --family view --mode signal \
  --recipe smoke --events 800 --background-events 40 --contract-only
```

The optional `tf_ab_conditional_stress.py` runner is self-locating and can run
in the existing TensorFlow container. It executes the vendored `PET` and
`MultiFold` loop for recoil-cloud A and the same cloud plus reconstructed-muon
globals B on the analytic fixture. It is an experimental synthetic closure
test, not publication evidence or TF/PyTorch layer equivalence.

`xps2_adapter.py` opens user-staged `.npy` arrays read-only with memmap and
materializes at most a declared bounded packet. Its receipt says `w_reco` is
unavailable and that using `w_truth` on reco would be a downgraded proxy; it
cannot support a full-event/G2 claim.

`xps2_pilot.py` can execute that explicitly downgraded, bounded recoil-only
engine pilot. It uses `w_truth` as the unavailable reco-weight proxy, the
precomputed xps2 measured target, no literal background inventory, no event
globals/types/views, and a boolean mask derived from the historical producer's
zero padding. Its runtime/tail evidence cannot be used as typed-token,
full-event, G2, or publication evidence. Selection and estimator seeds are
separate so retraining comparisons can hold the sampled rows fixed; `--seed`
is retained only as a coupled legacy-smoke shorthand.

`g2_memmap.py` is the production-size conversion seam for the still-unavailable
G2 NPZ. Given an externally receipt-bound input SHA-256 and size, it parses
safe NPY headers inside the ZIP, copies array payloads with a bounded buffer,
writes per-array dtype/shape/order/units/hashes, validates row-family and
legacy inventory-order hashes, and atomically publishes a readonly `.npy`
inventory. Interrupted conversions resume only after content verification.
The loader rechecks the source, completion marker, manifest, every array hash,
row family and identity hash before opening readonly memmaps and exposing
bounded windows; there is no hash-verification bypass. Progress and final
manifests are fingerprinted, and the input is rehashed before atomic
publication. Generated mini-packet tests are code-contract evidence, not G2
validation.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=nd-unfolding python3 -m pet2_torch.g2_memmap_cli convert \
  --source /receipt-bound/g2.npz --out /isolated/g2-npy \
  --expected-sha256 SHA256 --expected-size-bytes BYTES \
  --timestamp-utc YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ
PYTHONPATH=nd-unfolding python3 -m pet2_torch.g2_memmap_cli verify \
  --source /receipt-bound/g2.npz --directory /isolated/g2-npy
```

`public_gregor.py` can inspect an explicitly trusted, caller-checksummed `.pb`
using `torch.load(weights_only=True)` and emit row/schema/type/padding census
JSON. It never silently unpickles unknown files and remains MC-only.

Both diagnostics have JSON CLIs:

```bash

  --directory /staged/xps2_npy --max-rows 100000 --out /tmp/xps2_census.json
PYTHONPATH=nd-unfolding python3 -m pet2_torch.xps2_pilot \
  --directory /staged/xps2_npy --max-mc-rows 100000 \
  --max-data-rows 50000 --selection-seed 424242 \
  --estimator-seed 101 --out /isolated/xps2_pilot
PYTHONPATH=nd-unfolding python3 -m pet2_torch.public_gregor \
  --path /staged/public.pb --expected-sha256 SHA256 --trusted \
  --out /tmp/public_pb_census.json
```

Implementation review is complete. The PET2 continuation is ready for a clean source commit and isolated Delta validation. No provider, compute job, download, commit, or push was started.

### Findings

No unresolved BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.

Resolved MAJOR issues:

- Removed a cap-saturation pass/fail rule from carrier-shuffle that was not in the frozen preregistration. Cap telemetry remains reported.
- Made the muon carrier genuinely expressible by the model’s K=3 edge mechanism using two complete three-recoil neighborhoods.
- Removed the G2 loader’s hash-verification bypass and closed source-mutation/publication races.
- Replaced asserted parameter parity with computed model-configuration fingerprints, checked across all 90 arm results.

Resolved MINOR hardening:

- Fingerprinted and validated partial-conversion journals and final manifests.
- Revalidated resumed array paths, units, hashes, shapes, order, and source payload.
- Removed the production fault-injection argument; tests now inject faults by mocking.
- Strengthened certificates for split-local pairing, actual truth bytes, per-split chance AUC, bookkeeping exclusion, and exact pair mass.
- Made matched Delta execution reject dirty or non-git source checkouts.

The checkpoint compatibility design is internally consistent and needs no further edit. It remains documentation-only; legacy/corrected paths are distinct, diagnostic partial loads cannot become eligible, and arm F remains unavailable.
